author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: The child hierarchy kind has an unenforced direction and cardinality: 7 of 15 rows are inverted against the registry's own declaration and no channel, validator, or audit finding notices

The relationship registry declares a direction and a cardinality for the child hierarchy kind, and the corpus violates both without any surface objecting. src/sdk/relationships.ts declares child with hierarchyDirection source_parent, outgoing many, incoming one, and inverse parent. So a child row means the SOURCE is the parent of the target, and any single node may be named as a child by at most one parent.

Every child dependency row in the workspace was enumerated on 2026.7.28. There are exactly fifteen, and they are written in two opposite senses:

  8 rows obey the declaration. pm-7t04 names child->pm-0nia, child->pm-1265 and three siblings, and each of those targets carries the scalar parent pm-7t04. pm-v7dj does the same for three targets. Source is the parent, as declared.

  7 rows invert it. Each v1 delivery milestone names child->pm-j7a: pm-2xl, pm-u9r, pm-c0r, pm-54d, pm-f45, pm-b1w, pm-jiw. Read as declared, these seven assert that each milestone is the PARENT of the programme root, which is exactly backwards - pm-j7a is tagged milestone:root and area:program and each milestone separately carries the correctly directed implements->pm-j7a.

The inversion also breaks the declared cardinality. child declares incoming one, and pm-j7a has seven incoming child rows. Nothing enforces it: pm graph audit reports eleven findings, all severity info, and none of them is a direction violation or a cardinality violation.

The consequence is that a recorded hierarchy edge reaches no hierarchy consumer at all. Before this pass, with all seven child rows present and the scalar parent field empty on all seven, every consumer agreed on the wrong answer:

  pm list-all --parent pm-j7a       -> 3 items, none of them a milestone
  pm get pm-j7a --tree              -> count 3
  pm graph descendants pm-j7a       -> count 3

The seven scalar parent values have now been recorded from durable evidence, so those consumers report the full seventy-item origin epoch. That repairs the DATA and leaves the DEFECT: the write path accepted seven direction-inverted rows, no reader canonicalizes a child row into the parent channel, and no validation compares the two channels. The inverted rows are still present and are deliberately not deleted, because pm-flnefm establishes that the only available removal deletes every row matching an id and kind pair.

This is the third distinct instance of one class and none of the three subsumes the others. pm-jkbqt8 owns the ordering pair, where blocks and blocked_by schedule differently depending on which endpoint wrote the prerequisite. pm-rggtvd owns cycle detection over hierarchy-canonicalizing kinds, where mutual rows leave the graph provably inconsistent while every detector reports acyclic. This one is about a single hierarchy kind whose declared direction and declared cardinality are both unenforced, and whose rows are invisible to the scalar channel every hierarchy consumer actually reads. pm-4020c5 owns the lexicon of accepted spellings and is upstream of all three.

Writing a hierarchy dependency row is validated against the declared hierarchyDirection of its kind, and a row whose direction contradicts an existing scalar parent, or which would give a node more incoming child rows than the declared cardinality permits, is refused with a structured error naming both endpoints; Every hierarchy dependency kind resolves into the same internal parent relation that the scalar parent field feeds, so pm list --parent, pm get --tree, and the graph traversals return one answer regardless of which channel recorded the edge; pm validate reports a divergence between the dependency-row hierarchy and the scalar parent hierarchy as a data-quality warning class with the offending ids named, and the class starts at the seven known inverted rows so the count can only shrink; pm graph audit gains a direction-violation finding and a cardinality-violation finding at a severity above info, proven by a negative-control fixture that writes one inverted row and one over-cardinality row; A remediation path exists that retires a single misdirected row without deleting every row sharing its id and kind pair, closing the gap pm-flnefm records; The declared registry becomes the single source: a test asserts that every accepted hierarchy spelling has a declared direction and cardinality and that no code path canonicalizes a hierarchy kind by a rule not stated in the registry

message: File verified hierarchy direction and cardinality defect found by enumerating every child dependency row in the corpus
